Hi all —

Following up with the artifacts we can provide. I've attached a draft diagram and the canonical policy (see attachments list at the bottom). High-level notes:

1) Control-plane vs data-plane separation- The control plane for Dedicated/Private is managed by Redwood's control-plane cluster in a separate VPC/tenant that has no outbound access to customer data networks. Management traffic (scheduling, kernel-level commands, model updates) traverses a dedicated control subnet; vertex agents authenticate to the control plane using mutual TLS and short-lived mTLS certificates issued by Redwood CA.

2) Egress policy model (canonical form)- We provide a canonical JSON manifest that maps service-role -> egress-allow list. Example snippet below (this is the canonical format we use for the SOC packet):

{
  "service_role": "inference-worker",
  "allowed_egress": [
    {"cidr": "0.0.0.0/0", "ports": "443", "purpose": "model checksum retrieval (CDN)"},
    {"cidr": "10.8.0.0/16", "ports": "53", "purpose": "internal DNS stub"}
  ]
}

Note: for reviewer consumption we will redact any customer-specific CIDR ranges and provide canonical ranges and a mapping table.

3) Evidence artifacts we can include- controlplane-separation-diagram.png (attached)
- egress-policy-canonical.json (attached)
- sandboxed-egress-matrix.csv (attached) — this maps a few representative tenant flows to observed egress targets and ports

4) Packet/log sample guidance- We can produce a short pcap showing an outbound TLS handshake from a sandbox tenant to a CDN endpoint with NAT translation. We'll mask downstream IPs and provide a correlating flow log for auditability.

Timeline: we will finalize the attachments and deliver a zipped SOC packet by Mon 2027-05-17 20:00 UTC. If you want the raw pcap earlier for inspection we can push that today but masked.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
